newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-PAKISTAN CRUISE TO WIN OVER WEST INDIES.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-PAKISTAN CRUISE TO WIN OVER WEST INDIES.

text.p: Pakistan cruised to victory over a depleted West Indies side by eight wickets in their limited overs World Series match at the Sydney Cricket Ground on Tuesday.
Pakistan cantered to 183 for two with 64 balls to spare after West Indies earlier collapsed to be 181 all out, losing eight wickets for 25 runs in their last 10 overs.
Each of Pakistan's top order batsmen scored runs freely against a West Indies bowling attack lacking much penetration and accuracy, with free-swinging opener Aamir Sohail top-scoring on 55.
West Indies, who had won their previous five matches in a row, chose to rest top batsman Brian Lara and key fast bowlers Courtney Walsh and Curtly Ambrose.

The elimination of Australia from the tri-nation competition's finals series on Sunday, the first time the host team has missed the finals since 1979/80, meant this game would have no effect on the tournament standings.
Pakistan also treated the game as a dress rehearsal for the first final on Saturday, resting young fast-bowler Mohammad Zahid and spinner Shahid Afridi.
Lara's absence showed after West Indies lost the toss and were put in to bat, with only fellow left-hander Shivnarine Chanderpaul able to compile a decent score.
When Chanderpaul fell for 72 with the score at 156, a middle order bereft of Lara collapsed.
Twenty-year-old off-spinner Saqlain Mushtaq and fit again fast bowler Waqar Younis ripped out the heart of West Indies' middle and lower order in the space of 10 overs.

Saqlain troubled the West Indies batsmen with his carefully flighted offspinners, taking three wickets for 11 runs in the space of five overs and ending with four for 17 from nine overs. He was later named man of the match.
Waqar Younis, who returned to the Pakistani team after three weeks off with a shoulder injury, was back to his devastating best.
He took three for 35 from his 10 overs and showed as the ball became worn late in the innings that he had not lost his ability to extract his trademark reverse-swing.
The final on Saturday in Sydney is the first of a best-of-three series.
